newsitem.title: GREECE: Poseidon, ATE still lead Greek bond fund returns.
newsitem.headline: Poseidon, ATE still lead Greek bond fund returns.

text.p: Poseidon was leading Greece's 38 bond funds with a year-to-date return of 12.64 percent banking on the Athens bourse's sharp rise and a 20 percent equity exposure.
The asset and return figures were made available by Alpha Trust's weekly report.
Poseidon topped other bond funds returning 0.64 percent followed by Cosmos with 0.59 percent and ATE Capital with 0.54 percent for the week March 28 to April 4.

"There is no secret about our success. About 20 percent of Poseidon's assets are invested in equities which are doing very well and 80 percent in FRNs and fixed coupon bonds," said a fund manager at Bank of Piraeus' mutual fund management company.
Poseidon belongs to the family of the Bank of Piraeus' mutual funds.
"Less than 2.0 percent of Poseidon's assets are invested in foreign equities," he said. "Poseidon had 30 percent of its assets in equities and the rest in bonds at the end of 1996."
The fund will reduce its exposure to equities to comply with capital market commission regulations by August 31. These allow no more than 10 percent of a bond fund's assets to be invested in stocks.
ATE Capital was in second place with a year-to-date return of 7.57 percent and Aspis income was trailing closely behind in third place with 7.18 percent.
A fund manager at ATE Capital said good management was the secret behind the fund's high return.

"We are currently invested about 5.0 percent in equities and 95 percent in bonds," said a fund manager at ATE Capital. "We realised hefty capital gains by reducing our stock holdings before the bourse's fall in early March."
* Returns are based on NAV on April 4, 1997
Returns are not adjusted for risk. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
